title: B2+ · L40 — Scientific vocabulary intro
description: Vocabulario cientifico basico: hypothesis, correlation, causation, peer review, replicability, evidence.

questions.prompt: En un debate sobre metodo cientifico se define el punto de partida.
questions.question: A 'hypothesis' is:
options: A proven, established fact.
A testable, falsifiable prediction to be investigated.
A personal opinion with no basis.
A blind guess or random speculation.
questions.explanation: Hypothesis /haɪˈpɒθəsɪs/ = prediccion testeable y falsable. Base del metodo cientifico. NO es opinion ni certeza — es punto de partida para experimento. Registro: cientifico-tecnico. Plural: 'hypotheses' /haɪˈpɒθəsiːz/. Familia: 'hypothesize' (verbo, plantear hipotesis), 'hypothetical' (adjetivo). Distincion clave con 'theory': hypothesis es UNA prediccion; theory es un marco explicativo amplio ya bien respaldado. Error hispano frecuente: escribir 'hipothesis' (sin la 'y') o pronunciar la 'h' como en espanol — es /h/ aspirada suave o silenciosa en algunos acentos.
examples: Our hypothesis is that sleep improves memory consolidation — we designed the study to test it. → hipotesis de investigacion
The hypothesis was rejected after the double-blind trial failed to show the predicted effect. → resultado negativo

questions.prompt: Un journalist confunde relacion estadistica con causa.
questions.question: 'Correlation' means:
options: Direct cause of one thing by another.
A statistical relationship in which two variables move together.
A logical contradiction between two claims.
Definitive proof of a scientific claim.
questions.explanation: Correlation = variables que se mueven juntas estadisticamente. NO implica causacion. 'Correlation is not causation' es principio central y el error mas comun en journalism cientifico y en debate cotidiano. Registro: cientifico-estadistico. Tipos: positiva (ambas suben), negativa (una sube, otra baja), cero (no hay relacion). Coeficiente de correlacion /r/ va de -1 a +1. Error hispano tipico: aceptar titulares que afirman causalidad basandose solo en correlation. Familia: 'correlate' (verbo), 'correlated' (adjetivo — 'strongly correlated with'), 'confounding variable' (variable que causa spurious correlation).
examples: There's a strong correlation between education and income, but the causal story is more complex. → matiz academico
Correlation is not causation — the single most-abused principle in policy debate. → advertencia critica

questions.statement: 'Peer review' means academic experts evaluate a paper anonymously before it's published in a journal.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Peer review = revision anonima por expertos del mismo campo (peers). Filtro de calidad del sistema de publicacion cientifica desde mediados del siglo XX. Formatos: single-blind (autor conoce reviewer? no), double-blind (ninguno conoce al otro), open (todos identificados). No es perfecto — no detecta fraude, tiene sesgos, es lento — pero es el standard actual. Registro: academico-cientifico. Termino relacionado: 'preprint' (paper subido antes de peer review, comun en arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv). Error hispano: pronunciar 'peer' como 'pier' (muelle) — en anglo suenan igual /pɪər/, no problema; pero escribir 'pair review' es error comun.
examples: Peer-reviewed research carries more weight than a pre-print, though pre-prints move faster. → matiz academico
The paper is currently going through peer review — expected to publish by Q3. → estado de manuscrito

questions.prompt: Se debate la crisis de la ciencia moderna en un podcast academico.
questions.question: 'Replicability' in science refers to:
options: Copying raw data from another study.
The ability to repeat an experiment independently and obtain the same result.
Publishing the same finding in multiple journals.
The speed of a scientific process.
questions.explanation: Replicability = capacidad de que otros repitan el experimento y obtengan resultados similares. Distinta de 'reproducibility' (mismos datos, mismo analisis, mismo resultado — mas debil). La CRISIS DE REPLICABILIDAD (2010s presente) revelo que muchos hallazgos clasicos en psychology, medicine, cancer research no se replican. Registro: cientifico-metodologico. Palabras clave del debate: p-hacking, publication bias, HARKing (Hypothesizing After Results Known). Error hispano frecuente: confundir 'replicable' con 'replicable' — se pronuncia /ˈreplɪkəbl/ o /rɪˈplɪkəbl/, no como en espanol.
examples: Without replicability, findings are just anecdotes with better formatting. → critica dura
Many landmark psychology studies failed subsequent replication attempts — the field is still recovering. → contexto historico

questions.text: The findings are statistically significant but should be interpreted with caution due to the small sample size.
questions.explanation: Frase academica cientifica canonica. 'Statistically significant', 'interpreted with caution', 'small sample size' — todas colocaciones precisas del discurso empirico. Feature de connected speech: 'statistically significant' encadena /stəˈtɪstɪkli sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt/ sin pausa; 'interpreted with' /ɪnˈtɜːprɪtɪd wɪð/ con /t/ intermedia debil, casi flap en americano. 'Sample size' se pronuncia con acento en 'sample'. 'Statistically significant' NO es sinonimo de 'important' — significa solo 'improbable por azar bajo H0'.
examples: Results are significant (p < 0.05) but require independent replication before being called conclusive. → matiz cientifico
The effect is statistically meaningful but modest in magnitude — practical significance is another question. → analisis maduro

questions.prompt: Un ensayo clinico se explica en un briefing medico.
questions.question: 'Control group' means:
options: The group of scientists who control the experiment.
The group that does NOT receive the intervention, used for comparison.
Any small subset of participants.
The group with the most experimental control.
questions.explanation: Control group = grupo comparativo que NO recibe la intervencion (o recibe placebo). Sin control group, no puedes atribuir efectos al tratamiento — podria ser efecto placebo, regresion a la media, o cambios naturales. Base absoluta del experimental design. Registro: cientifico-metodologico. Gold standard: RCT (Randomized Controlled Trial) con doble ciego (double-blind). Familia: 'placebo', 'sham surgery', 'active control' (comparar contra tratamiento existente en vez de placebo). Error hispano: 'control' aqui NO es 'controlar' sino 'referencia comparativa'.
examples: The control group received a placebo pill identical in appearance to the actual drug. → diseno experimental
Without a control group, causal claims are impossible — you just have before-and-after correlation. → limite metodologico

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino cientifico con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Vocabulario cientifico esencial. Notas de precision: 'data' es tecnicamente plural en anglo formal ('the data ARE clear'), aunque el uso singular ('the data IS clear') se ha extendido. 'Bias' se refiere a error SISTEMATICO (no aleatorio) — confirmation bias, selection bias, survivorship bias son categorias tecnicas. 'Sample size' correlaciona con statistical power: mas grande = mas capacidad de detectar efectos reales. Registro: cientifico-tecnico. Error hispano frecuente: usar 'datum' (singular latino) o 'datas' (plural incorrecto) — ambos suenan raros.
examples: Confirmation bias is when we unconsciously favor evidence that supports our prior beliefs. → definicion tecnica
A larger sample size increases statistical power to detect true effects. → principio estadistico

questions.target: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence — that's a bedrock principle of science.
questions.explanation: Cita atribuida a Carl Sagan, aforismo cientifico universal. 'Bedrock principle' = principio fundamental (metafora geologica: la roca sobre la que se construye todo). Uso tipico: en discurso sobre pseudociencia, teorias conspirativas, medicina alternativa. Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'evidence,', tono descendente en 'bedrock principle of science'. Contracciones: 'that's' obligatoria. Registro: divulgacion cientifica seria, TED, podcasts intelectuales. Estructura retorica: la repeticion de 'extraordinary' crea eco memorable. Formula transferible: la afirmacion mas grande, la evidencia debe ser proporcionalmente mas robusta.
examples: Big claims need big evidence — you can't overturn established science with a single anecdote. → principio critico
The burden of evidence scales with the boldness of the claim — that's just epistemic honesty. → rigor cientifico

questions.prompt: En una discusion sobre epistemologia se distingue evidencia de opinion.
questions.question: 'Empirical evidence' is:
options: Evidence based purely on opinion.
Evidence based on observation, experiment, or measurement.
Historical or anecdotal evidence only.
Legal or courtroom evidence.
questions.explanation: Empirical /ɛmˈpɪrɪkl/ = basado en observacion, experimento, o medicion directa. Opuesto: teorico, especulativo, a priori. Central en ciencia moderna desde Bacon y el metodo empirico. Registro: cientifico-filosofico. Familia: 'empiricism' (empirismo, doctrina filosofica), 'empirically' (adverbio — 'empirically demonstrated'), 'empiricist'. Error hispano frecuente: escribir 'empirical' con doble 'p' o pronunciar la 'e' inicial como en espanol. Suena /ɛm-/. Otro matiz: 'anecdotal evidence' NO es empirical evidence en sentido cientifico — es un caso aislado sin control.
examples: The claim lacks any empirical support — it rests entirely on intuition and analogy. → critica cientifica
Empirical evidence trumps theoretical elegance when the two conflict — that's the basic rule. → jerarquia epistemica

questions.statement: 'Falsifiable' means a hypothesis CAN be proven wrong by evidence — a key criterion for it being scientific.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Karl Popper (1934): falsifiability = criterio de demarcacion entre ciencia y no-ciencia. Si una hipotesis no puede ser refutada POR PRINCIPIO por ninguna observacion, no es cientifica — puede ser metafisica, ideologia, poesia, pero no ciencia. Ejemplo canonico: 'existen dragones invisibles e indetectables' — no falsifiable, por tanto no cientifico. Registro: filosofico-cientifico. Critica: la demarcacion de Popper es debatida por filosofos posteriores (Kuhn, Lakatos, Feyerabend), pero sigue siendo el criterio mas influyente. Error hispano: confundir 'falsifiable' con 'falso' — significa 'capaz de ser refutado', no 'ya refutado'.
examples: 'Invisible undetectable dragons exist' is not falsifiable — hence not scientific in Popper's sense. → ejemplo clasico
A good hypothesis makes predictions that could, in principle, prove it wrong. → criterio central

questions.prompt: En un debate sobre evidence-based medicine se ubica el nivel mas alto.
questions.question: 'Meta-analysis' combines:
options: The results of one single major study.
Results from multiple studies to reach stronger, aggregated conclusions.
Only theoretical arguments without data.
Interviews with subject-matter experts.
questions.explanation: Meta-analysis /ˌmetəəˈnæləsɪs/ = agregacion estadistica de multiples estudios sobre la misma pregunta. Aumenta poder estadistico y reduce el ruido de estudios individuales. Gold standard cuando disponible y bien hecho. En la jerarquia de evidencia esta en la cima (junto con systematic reviews). Registro: cientifico-clinico. Familia: 'systematic review' (revision cualitativa sistematica; a menudo incluye meta-analysis), 'forest plot' (grafico caracteristico). LIMITE: 'garbage in, garbage out' — si los estudios individuales son malos, el meta-analysis tambien. Error hispano: escribir 'meta analisis' sin guion o 'metanalysis' — en anglo el standard es 'meta-analysis'.
examples: A meta-analysis of forty studies confirmed the effect across populations. → evidencia agregada
Meta-analyses sit at the top of the evidence hierarchy when the constituent studies are sound. → matiz metodologico

questions.text: The study's methodology was rigorous, but its conclusions may not generalize beyond the specific population sampled.
questions.explanation: Discurso cientifico maduro. 'Rigorous methodology' (colocacion), 'may not generalize' (hedge tecnico), 'population sampled' (termino estadistico). Reconoce validez interna sin sobreextender validez externa — marca de investigador honesto. Feature de connected speech: 'study's methodology' /ˈstʌdiz meθəˈdɒlədʒi/ con /z/ del possessive suavizado; 'may not generalize' /meɪ nɒt ˈdʒenrəlaɪz/ con /t/ final casi elidida delante de consonante. Registro: academico-empirico. Distincion clave: internal validity (correcto para esta muestra) vs external validity (generaliza a otras poblaciones).
examples: Strong internal validity, but external generalizability is limited to comparable populations. → matiz metodologico
The finding holds in this population; extrapolation beyond it is speculative until replicated. → cautela academica

questions.prompt: Analista epidemiologico explica por que dos variables correlacionan sin causar.
questions.question: 'Confounding variable' is:
options: A confused or unclear participant.
An unmeasured third factor that affects both variables being studied.
Any variable at all in the study.
A simple demographic metric.
questions.explanation: Confounder = variable oculta (a menudo no medida) que causa spurious correlation entre dos variables observadas. Ejemplo canonico: ventas de helado y ahogamientos correlacionan porque ambas dependen de la temperatura (verano) — la temperatura es el confounder. Central en analisis causal. Registro: estadistico-epidemiologico. Tecnicas para controlar confounders: randomization, stratification, regression, propensity score matching, instrumental variables. Error hispano: llamarlo 'confusor' es traduccion tecnica valida pero en anglo tecnico casi siempre se dice 'confounder' o 'confounding variable'.
examples: Age is a common confounder in health studies — must be controlled for statistically. → variable clasica
Confounding variables can create the illusion of causation where none exists. → advertencia metodologica

questions.statement: 'Scientific consensus' means literally all scientists agree — an absolute unanimous standard.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Scientific consensus = acuerdo entre la GRAN MAYORIA de expertos del campo, no unanimidad literal. Siempre existen dissidentes en cualquier tema — la ciencia no funciona por votacion sino por convergencia de evidencia. Consensus fuerte + evidence robusta = practical certainty. Error tipico en debate publico: presentar la existencia de UN cientifico disidente como evidencia de que 'no hay consensus' — es manipulacion retorica. Registro: cientifico-comunicacional. Ejemplos de fuerte consensus: evolucion biologica, cambio climatico antropogenico, seguridad de vacunas, edad del universo. Error hispano: interpretar 'consensus' como 'unanimidad' — no lo es en ningun campo.
examples: There's overwhelming scientific consensus on human-caused climate change — 97%+ of climatologists. → dato clasico
Consensus doesn't require unanimity — it means the community has converged on an explanation. → distincion tecnica

questions.target: The evidence, while suggestive, doesn't yet meet the threshold for a firm causal claim — we need larger studies and independent replication.
questions.explanation: Discurso cientifico riguroso. 'Suggestive' (hedge: sugiere pero no prueba), 'threshold' (umbral tecnico), 'firm causal claim' (jerga de causal inference), 'larger studies and independent replication' (que hace falta). Modelo de comunicacion cientifica madura tipo journalist cientifico serio. Ritmo natural: pausas breves tras cada clausula, enfasis tonico en 'doesn't yet', tono descendente y firme en 'replication'. Contracciones: 'doesn't' obligatoria. Registro: cientifico-comunicativo, ideal para explicar preliminary findings sin sobre-vender ni sub-vender.
examples: Promising results, but far from conclusive at this stage — the mechanism is still unclear. → matiz cientifico
Preliminary — awaiting independent replication before drawing firm conclusions about causality. → cautela profesional
